data.narrative:
Voya Energy is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Richard Wang, Matt Horton, and Steven Kaye that has raised $13M to date. The valuation universe comprises 9 private peers in Climate & Energy alongside 1 public comparable (Lnza), though narrower peer filtering by stage and valuation tier yielded insufficient datapoints for a median-based approach.

Given the constraint on peer density, Stage-Progression methodology provides the primary valuation signal. Applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $13M total raised as a baseline proxy yields $32M. This method is most applicable when direct public or same-stage private comps are sparse, as here. A sensitivity band around this midpoint—$28M (low) to $37M (high)—reflects reasonable variance in step-up multiplier assumptions (2.1x to 2.9x).

The valuation range of $28M–$37M, with a median of $32M, rests on a single methodological pillar. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for this subsector and stage, product-market fit validation, and capital efficiency relative to Climate & Energy peers. Additional comps or near-term funding signals would strengthen conviction. The peer universe (Helion, Redwood Materials, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen) suggests the sector attracts substantial capital, but without same-stage private transactions in the dataset, this valuation carries meaningful model risk.
